title: Gripper calibration drifts after cold restart on AMR-7
author: Dana Okafor
text:
After a cold restart the gripper encoder offset falls back to the factory default, so the first 10-20 picks miss the tote.

Repro: power-cycle an AMR-7 unit, then run the pick test.
Suspect: the calibrated offset is only kept in RAM and never written to flash.

comments.author: Dana Okafor
comments.text: Fix in review: write the encoder offset to flash at the end of calibration. Ships in firmware 4.8.1.

title: AMR-7 gripper loses calibration after overnight power cycle
author: Eli Brooks
text: Night shift reports missed picks on AMR-7-04, AMR-7-09 and AMR-7-11 every morning after the units are powered down overnight. Operators have to re-home the gripper by hand before the first wave.

comments.author: Eli Brooks
comments.text: Attached the night-shift logs from Bob. The calibration offset reads as factory default after each power-up.

title: Replace Friday fleet-wide firmware push with a staged canary rollout
author: Farah Haddad
text:
Approved by Alice on 6 Oct in #eng-fleet. From Monday 12 Oct every firmware release goes to a canary ring (5% of the fleet, spread across sites) for 24 hours before the full fleet.

- [ ] Pick the canary ring units
- [ ] Auto-halt the rollout if the pick error rate rises by more than 0.5 points
- [ ] Update the Firmware Release Runbook in Notion
- [ ] First release through the ring: 4.8.1

comments.author: Dana Okafor
comments.text: Canary ring picked: AMR-7-02 and AMR-7-17, one per site.

title: Aisle 12 cycle count: keep robots out 22:00-02:00
author: Bob Rivera
text: Quarterly cycle count in aisle 12. Geofence aisle 12 for all AMR-7 units from 22:00 to 02:00 tonight and lift it after the count.

title: Pick-rate dashboard shows night shift in UTC instead of local time
author: Eli Brooks
text: Night shift pick rates are bucketed by UTC day, so one shift is split across two days.

comments.author: Eli Brooks
comments.text: Fixed: buckets use warehouse local time now.
